roadmap_item: R4 (Coulomb collisions) of modern/docs/pic2d-physics-completeness-audit.md section 5; gap (d) of section 4.d
status: code-and-tests-complete; shakedown-only; no preregistered run; physics not validated against a discharge
supersedes: modern/spec/pic2d/pic2d-model-v2.3.json and pic2d-model-v2.2.json (every v2.0.x / v2.1 / v2.2 / v2.3 physics, gate, time-step, checkpoint and artifact contract is kept; this file adds ONE selectable physics option, the Coulomb collision operator coulomb_v1, its ledger tallies and its diagnostics)
unchanged_from_v2_3: domain, field, time step, Boris push, ion subcycling, fixed-point deposition, bilinear gather, dielectric surface-charge closure, wall-ion recycling, cathode models, gates (v2.0.3 / v2.0.4 / v2.0.6 floors), energy ledger W convention (v2.0.6), momentum ledger keys of v2.0 / v2.2 / v2.3, SEE (v2.2.0), xenon collision set (v2.3.0), Poisson solvers, frame recorder, checkpoint binding (the Coulomb tallies travel as extra cumulative keys only when the operator is on)
what_changed: Coulomb collisions between the charged species: electron-electron and electron-ion binary collisions (ion-ion optional, off by default) by the Takizuka-Abe (1977) pairing inside each mesh cell with the Nanbu (1997) cumulative scattering angle, applied every cycle_steps steps with Delta t_c = cycle_steps x dt to the pushed populations (after the Boris push and wall absorption, before the ion MCC / anomalous / electron MCC stages and that step's births), on both backends.

Ledgers: extra cumulative keys coulomb_{ee,ei,ii}_{pairs,s_sum,large_s,lnl_sum}, coulomb_electron_cycles, coulomb_ion_cycles, coulomb_cycles, pz_coulomb (the pair momentum change, zero by construction), ke_coulomb_j (the relativistic pair kinetic-energy change of an operator that conserves the CLASSICAL pair energy exactly - O(v^2/c^2) of the redistributed energy, ~1e-9 of K_e per record - booked as an energy source so the particle-side identity closes to round-off; there is no physical energy source or sink). Series: a 'coulomb' block (mean nu_ee, nu_ei, nu_ii, mean s and ln Lambda per pair, the fraction of pairs with s > 1, the interval's electron-neutral elastic frequency and nu_ee / nu_en); currents_a gains coulomb_nu_ee_mean_per_s / coulomb_nu_ei_mean_per_s; ledger gains interval_coulomb_ke_j; the momentum block (plume domains) gains coulomb_momentum_rate_n and the residual carries pz_coulomb.

Window diagnostics (additive sums, present only with the operator on): per-cell sum of s and pair count for e-e and e-i and the electron-seconds sum_cycles N_e Delta t_c, stored in the node layout (cell (i, j) at node index (i, j), last row / column zero) -> maps.npz / frames gain coulomb_nu_ee_per_s, coulomb_nu_ei_per_s (window-mean frequencies per cell; the per-cusp reading is the electron-weighted column mean at the cusp planes, coulomb.column_frequency_profile) and coulomb_mean_s_ee.

Identity: PIC2DConfig.coulomb = CoulombConfig enters to_dict() and therefore config_sha256 with every parameter (enabled, species pairs, cycle_steps, Coulomb-logarithm mode / fixed value / floor, temperature floor, and the method description); absent = collisionless charged species and every recorded identity unchanged.

Warp backend: new kernel module warp_coulomb (cell sort as a slot PERMUTATION, per-cell prepare, like-pair and unlike-pair kernels) launched after the push on Coulomb cycles; a sixth per-step RNG stream (seed-table column 5, stream id 6) appended without changing columns 0-4; the CUDA-graph key gains the coulomb-cycle flag; the stage owns its statistics and window arrays (read at the host sync / with the diagnostics).

Runner: numerics.coulomb = CoulombConfig fields selects the operator; records_to_arrays carries the coulomb_* series columns, interval_coulomb_ke_j and momentum_coulomb_momentum_rate_n (NaN / absent on older records).

coulomb_v1.name: coulomb_v1

method.pairing: Takizuka & Abe 1977 (doi:10.1016/0021-9991(77)90099-7): the alive particles of a species are grouped by mesh cell; like particles are paired at random inside their cell (a uniform random permutation of the cell's members); an odd count uses the triplet rule - members 0, 1, 2 collide pairwise (0,1), (0,2), (1,2) with Delta t_c / 2 each, the rest in consecutive pairs with Delta t_c - so every particle experiences one full time step of scattering; a cell with one particle does not collide. Electron-ion: every electron of a cell collides once with ion (l + shift) mod N_i (a random shift per cell) at the field density n_i = N_i W / V_cell; the ions therefore collide N_e / N_i times on average - the Takizuka-Abe rule for unequal groups gives both species the physical rate (the electron's rate is proportional to n_i, the ion's to n_e).
method.angle: Nanbu 1997 (doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.55.4642) cumulative scattering angle: f(chi) proportional to exp(A cos chi) with coth A - 1/A = exp(-s), s = (ln Lambda / 4 pi) (q_a q_b / (epsilon_0 m_ab))^2 n_field Delta t / g^3 (m_ab the reduced mass, g the relative speed); <1 - cos chi> = 1 - exp(-s) exactly, i.e. <chi^2> = 2 s for small s = the Takizuka-Abe variance <tan^2(chi/2)> = s / 2; valid for any s (isotropic as s -> infinity). A(s): 1 / (1 - exp(-s)) for s < 0.2 (exact mean; cos chi = 1 + ln(U) / A), the Perez et al. 2012 (doi:10.1063/1.4742167) polynomial for 1/A on 0.2 <= s < 3, A = 3 exp(-s) on 3 <= s < 6 (cos chi = ln(exp(-A) + 2 U sinh A) / A), isotropic cos chi = 2 U - 1 for s >= 6; uniform azimuth. Sampler means verified on every branch (tests).
method.kinematics: exact centre-of-mass rotation of the relative velocity (Takizuka-Abe Eqs. 4-6): v_a' = v_a + (m_b / M) Delta u, v_b' = v_b - (m_a / M) Delta u with |u + Delta u| = |u|; equal macro weights for all species (macro_weight is shared), so the pair conserves momentum and classical kinetic energy to round-off without the Nanbu-Yonemura weighted-particle correction. The velocity components (v_r, v_theta, v_z) of a pair are treated as Cartesian components of one local frame (the same convention as the MCC isotropic scatter): v_z momentum is conserved exactly (pz_coulomb = 0 by construction); a zero relative speed leaves the pair unchanged.
method.coulomb_logarithm: NRL Plasma Formulary (2019) from the cell's own density n = N W / V_cell and temperature T = m (<v^2> - |<v>|^2) / (3 e) over the cell's alive members (n in cm^-3, T in eV inside the formulas): e-e 23.5 - ln(n^1/2 T^-5/4) - [1e-5 + (ln T - 2)^2 / 16]^1/2; e-i 23 - ln(n^1/2 Z T_e^-3/2) for T_e < 10 Z^2 eV else 24 - ln(n^1/2 / T_e) (uses the ELECTRON cell moments; Z = 1); i-i 23 - ln[(1 / T_i) (2 n_i / T_i)^1/2]. Cutoffs: the temperature floor min_temperature_ev (0.01 eV) guards ln(0) in cells of 2-3 particles (the estimate is noisy there; the dependence is logarithmic), the floor coulomb_log_floor (2.0) bounds the value from below; the density argument is the cell's, so an empty or one-particle cell never enters. coulomb_log_fixed replaces the local value by a constant (tests; declared in the identity). At the audit's plateau (1e18 m^-3, 7 eV) both electron logarithms are 12.1.
method.cycle: cycle_steps k (default 10): the operator runs at the end of every k-th step with Delta t_c = k dt (the ion-subcycle phase rule (step + 1) mod k == 0). Sizing: at 1.4 ps and the ext-val point (n_e 1e19, T_e 5 eV, ln Lambda ~10) nu_ee dt ~ 4e-5, so k = 10 gives a per-cycle deflection parameter s ~ 4e-4 at the peak (far inside the small-angle regime the once-per-cycle pairing assumes; the mean over pairs is larger because s is proportional to 1/g^3) and k dt = 14 ps is under half the 33 um cell crossing of a 5 eV electron (33 ps), so a particle's collision partners are its cell neighbours; at our 1e18 plateau s is 10x smaller. The runtime check is recorded, not gated: the series carries the mean s per pair and the fraction of pairs with s > 1 (the once-per-cycle pairing is coarse there; Nanbu's angle stays exact); k = 1 and k = 2 relax an anisotropic population at the same rate within statistics (test).
method.species_pairs: electron_electron and electron_ion default on; ion_ion default off: with the local ion 'temperature' set by the birth-potential spread of the accelerated population (10-50 eV), nu_ii / nu_ee = (m_e / M)^1/2 (T_e / T_i)^3/2 ~ 1e-3 and nu_ii x (ion transit 2.4 us) << 1; in the cold anode-side population nu_ii tau can reach 0.1-1 but those ions are unaccelerated and their thermalisation at 0.03 eV changes nothing the model claims (S, I_d, IEDF, wall energies). The operator is implemented (the like-pair kernel on the ion arrays with the i-i logarithm) and tested for conservation and determinism; switching it on is a declared identity change.
method.rng: CPU reference: np.random.default_rng([seed, step, 6]) per Coulomb cycle (stream ids 1 MCC, 2 injection, 3 anomalous, 4 ion-neutral MCC, 5 SEE, 6 Coulomb). Warp: seed-table column 5 (stream id 6, stream_seed(seed, step, 6)); keys inside the column: cell index (electron shuffles / shift), n_cells + cell index (ion shuffles), 2 n_cells + sorted position (e-e pairs), + capacity (e-i, keyed on the sorted ION position whose thread loops over its electrons), + 2 capacity (i-i). Columns 0-4 are unchanged, so every configuration without the operator replays bitwise; parity between the backends is distributional.

gpu_pairing.statement: The base RNG contract keys every per-particle stream on the particle's SLOT index; physically sorting the arrays would change every draw (the perf-audit lesson). The stage therefore builds, per cycle, a cell-sorted PERMUTATION of the alive slots and pairs through it; no particle is moved.
gpu_pairing.kernels: cell_kernel (cell of each alive slot; provisional position from an integer atomic), exclusive scan of the cell counts (segment starts), scatter_kernel (provisional segment list), rank_kernel (rank = number of same-cell alive slots with a smaller slot index -> a deterministic segment order = slot order, whatever the atomic arrival order was), prepare_kernel (one thread per cell: moments in sorted order, Fisher-Yates shuffle of the segment, the e-i shift draw, the electron-seconds window sum), cycle_kernel (electron / ion counts of the cycle), like_kernel (one thread per sorted position; the first member performs the pair; the thread of member 0 runs the odd-count triplet sequentially), unlike_kernel (one thread per sorted ION position; it loops over its electrons l = l0 + m N_i sequentially - an electron belongs to exactly one ion, so no two threads write the same particle).
gpu_pairing.graph: every launch has a fixed shape (the array capacities / the cell count) and reads only device arrays (slot counts, alive flags, the seed table, the step counter); counts.zero_() and the scan are the operations the MCC spawn already captures; the graph key gains the Coulomb-cycle flag (at most 2x the step variants). Verified: CUDA graph vs direct launches bitwise with the operator on (e-e + e-i + i-i), same seed replays the same state (tests on the box).
gpu_pairing.cost: the rank kernel reads a cell segment per particle: O(sum over cells of k^2) with k the cell occupancy (35 average, ~150-250 in the dense channel cells of the 33 um protocol) - the dominant Coulomb cost; measured on the H100: see cost.
gpu_pairing.work_arrays: per species: cell, provisional position, provisional list, sorted permutation, cell-of-sorted (int32 x capacity each, allocated with the particle scratch and re-captured with it); per cell: counts / starts (n_cells + 1), density, temperature, shift; the stage's 17-slot statistics array and five per-cell window sums.

ledger.energy: The operator is elastic in the classical sense (pair energy conserved to round-off). The ledger's kinetic energy is relativistic ((gamma - 1) m c^2), so the pairs change it by O((v/c)^2) of the energy they redistribute: this remainder is tallied as ke_coulomb_j and booked as a source, so the identity dKE = field work + injected - absorbed + born - W sum n E + emitted + ke_coulomb closes to round-off with the operator on (tests: cpu, warp-cpu, cuda). At 10 eV the remainder is ~1e-9 of K_e per record - nothing a residual-power gate can see. No physical energy term is added.
ledger.momentum: pz_coulomb = W sum over pairs of (m_a dv_a,z + m_b dv_b,z): zero by construction (the operator conserves the pair momentum); it enters the momentum-ledger residual and the plume momentum block as coulomb_momentum_rate_n; the discharge test bounds it at 1e-9 of the represented momentum per cycle.
ledger.counts: coulomb_ee_pairs / coulomb_ei_pairs / coulomb_ii_pairs (binary collisions; triplet sub-pairs count each), coulomb_*_s_sum (sum of the pair deflection parameter), coulomb_*_large_s (pairs with s > 1), coulomb_*_lnl_sum (sum of ln Lambda), coulomb_electron_cycles / coulomb_ion_cycles (sum over cycles of the alive counts), coulomb_cycles.
ledger.frequencies: TWO definitions are recorded. (1) The operator's pair-mean deflection rate nu_ee = 2 sum s_ee / (sum_cycles N_e Delta t_c) (a pair gives both electrons s), nu_ei = sum s_ei / (sum_cycles N_e Delta t_c), nu_ii likewise with N_i - per record from the ledger differences (coulomb.coulomb_frequencies), per cell from the window sums (maps): the average over the formed pairs of nu_pair = (lnL / 4 pi)(q_a q_b / eps0 m_ab)^2 n / g^3, whose 1/g^3 weighting is dominated by the slowest pairs (the population mean diverges logarithmically; the sample mean grows with the sample size) - it is the realised deflection statistic of the operator, typically 10x the thermal rate, NOT the audit's collision frequency. (2) nu_e_spitzer_peak_per_s: the NRL electron collision rate 2.91e-6 n lnL T^-3/2 at the record's peak node with the e-e logarithm (the audit's gap-(d) definition; the shakedown readings add it at the window's peak cell and per cusp column). nu_en (elastic) is the MCC elastic tally of the interval per electron (n_g is uniform in the channel); both ratios to it are recorded - nu_e_spitzer_peak_over_nu_en is the audit's number.

identity.how: PIC2DConfig.to_dict()['coulomb'] = CoulombConfig.to_dict() (model, enabled, electron_electron, electron_ion, ion_ion, cycle_steps, coulomb_log mode, coulomb_log_fixed, coulomb_log_floor, min_temperature_ev, method block); present only when a CoulombConfig is given (enabled = False records the block without collisions: a different identity from both 'absent' and 'on').
identity.off_is_bitwise: coulomb = None: to_dict unchanged (the v2.2.0 SEE-off pin 9690a3bf... re-asserted in the v2.4.0 tests), no ledger key, no window sum, no map, no record block; the fixed 300-step run of the v2.2.0 pin reproduces its integer tallies and counts on cpu and warp-cpu; SEED_STREAMS 5 -> 6 appends the Coulomb column without changing columns 0-4 (stream_seed per column), so the Warp seeds of MCC / injection / anomalous / ion-MCC / SEE are unchanged.

predeclared_expectations.reference: ss-v4 33 um channel-only plateau 0d228ad2 (I_d 3.80 mA, S 3.60e16 /s, n_g 3.19e19, peak n_e 1.29e18, T_e,peak 5.58 eV) and, for the code-to-code comparison, the ext-val point (Brandt 2016: n_e ~1e19); all statements are directions and rough magnitudes from the audit (sections 4.d, 5, 9) - a result of the opposite sign is a finding, not a tuning target
predeclared_expectations.frequencies: nu_ee / nu_en 0.15-0.4 at the 1e18 plateau (peak 1.3-1.6e18) and 1.4-3.4 at 1e19 (NRL nu_e = 2.91e-6 n lnL T^-3/2 against nu_en = n_g k_el ~ 8e6 s^-1 at n_g 3e19); the recorded nu_ee_over_nu_en of the series and the per-cusp column means of coulomb_nu_ee_per_s are the readings
predeclared_expectations.ionisation: S UP 5-20 % at our plateau (the inelastic-depleted tail is refilled: k_iz is exponentially sensitive to the tail at T_e 5-7 eV), more at 1e19; gross utilisation follows; the n_g fixed point moves down with S
predeclared_expectations.temperature: T_e,peak DOWN ~5 % (tail energy shared); EEDF closer to Maxwellian
predeclared_expectations.current: I_d UP a few %; classical cross-field transport from e-i collisions stays 2-3 orders below the Bohm term (no visible change of the cusp loss structure from Coulomb alone)
predeclared_expectations.ledger: residual-power gate behaviour unchanged (the operator is elastic; ke_coulomb_j is booked); pz_coulomb round-off
predeclared_expectations.not_expected: no change of any electron-neutral rate at fixed EEDF; no change of the ion dynamics beyond the e-i momentum handed to the ions (2 m_e / M per collision)

verification.tests: tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_v24_coulomb.py (17): pair kinematics exact (relative speed, momentum, classical energy, applied angle, uniform azimuth, degenerate u_perp = 0 branch, zero relative speed); Nanbu sampler mean on every branch + the small-s <chi^2> = 2 s and the isotropic limit; the deflection parameter formula; NRL logarithms and the numeric forms of the reference rates; identity (every parameter; off / disabled / on distinct; the coulomb_step phase rule); Coulomb off = the v2.2.0 pin (identity 9690a3bf, ledger keys, window sums, the 300-step tallies on cpu and warp-cpu, SEED_STREAMS 6 with columns 0-4 unchanged); Trubnikov relaxation of a bi-Maxwellian (A = -0.5 and -0.14) within 10 % of the path-integrated NRL rate on the numpy reference and the Warp stage (cpu device; cuda when present); Spitzer / Lorentz slowing-down of a drifting electron population on cold Xe+ (bounded per-electron expectation within 10 %; initial slope = Braginskii 2.91e-6 n lnL T^-3/2 within 10 %; ion momentum gain = electron loss); two-temperature e-i exchange across the mass ladder 10 / 100 / 1000 m_e with cold ions (the Landau integral the formed pairs realise = Spitzer's nu_eps within 8 %), the realised exchange = the pair expectation within 15 % (warm ions, 10 m_e), the heavy-ion bound (xenon, ions at rest: |dE_e| / E_e < 4 x 4 m_e / M and < 1e-4 per cycle; the electrons cool, the ions warm); sub-cycle invariance k = 1 vs 2 (same initial particles; log decays within 0.04) and same-seed replay; discharge conservation on cpu / warp-cpu / cuda (pz_coulomb < 1e-9 of the represented momentum, ke_coulomb_j < 1e-4 K_e, particle-side identity to 1e-6, record block, currents, ledger term, maps in the node layout, frames' interval maps, provenance); warp vs numpy in distribution; CUDA graph vs direct bitwise with e-e + e-i + i-i on and same-seed replay; cuda stage vs cpu stage counts within 2 %; runner block + series columns.
verification.relaxation_numbers: numpy reference at N = 200k, lnL 10, n 1e21 m^-3: Trubnikov log-decay ratio 0.963 (T_par 8 / T_perp 4 eV) and 1.048 (5.5 / 4.75 eV) with mean s 0.043; Lorentz drift decay measured / expected 0.959 over 300 cycles (N 200k); per-cycle realised e-i energy exchange / Landau expectation 1.003 (m_i = 10 m_e, 200 cycles, N 100k); the Landau expectation of the formed pairs at t = 0 is 0.957 of Spitzer at mean s 0.11 (the finite-s factor (1 - exp(-s)) / s), 1.0 as s -> 0. Without like-particle collisions the two-temperature decay falls below Spitzer's (0.74 at m_i = 10 m_e) because the e-i operator alone does not keep the electrons Maxwellian - physical, and the reason the test compares against the Landau integral of the actual distribution.
verification.limits: The Nanbu angle is exact for any s, but the once-per-cycle pairing with a fixed partner is coarse for s >~ 1: the relaxation rate then falls below the analytic one (0.79-0.83 of Trubnikov at mean s 0.3-0.8 in the development runs). The per-cycle s statistics are recorded so a protocol can be checked; the default k = 10 keeps the peak-cell s ~4e-4 at 1e19.

cost.measured_h100_contended: experiments/pic2d_coulomb_v1_shakedown/cost.json (2026-09-04 19:26 UTC, 5 other MPS clients at 100 %): 4.5 M synthetic plateau load (2.25 M e- + 2.25 M Xe+) on the 90 x 720 grid - Coulomb cycle 4.49 ms (cell sort of both species 1.14, prepare + pair kernels 3.34); inside the captured step 11.45 vs 6.62 ms -> 4.82 ms per cycle = 0.48 ms/step amortised over k = 10 = +7.3 % of the contended step (+73 % at k = 1); the shakedown's step rate 4.79 vs the off twin's 4.52 ms/step (+6 %). Under MPS small kernels inflate 7-10x and large ones 1.1-1.4x, so the ratio is the figure to quote until a solo probe.
cost.a_priori: the audit's estimate was +15-30 % per step if every step, +2-3 % amortised over 10-20 steps

coulomb_v1.shakedown: experiments/pic2d_coulomb_v1_shakedown/ (the R3 shakedown protocol - ss-v4 33 um with xe_collision_set_v2 - plus numerics.coulomb; 100 000 steps through finalize + assess on the Lambda H100 as an extra MPS client on 2026-09-04 19:27-19:37 UTC, code e0d0a28a; NOT a result). Readings (README): target_steps_reached, 4.79 ms/step, verdict no_plateau, residual window +0.14 % (off twin +0.09 %), pz_coulomb 5e-29 kg m/s and ke_coulomb_j 3.9e-16 J cumulative over 8.5e9 pair collisions; mean s per pair 6e-5 / 4.5e-5, pairs with s > 1 at the 1e-6 level; Spitzer nu_e at the window's peak cell 2.8e5 /s (n_e 1.7e17, T_e 8.2 eV, lnL 13.2) vs nu_en 1.17e7 /s -> 0.024 in the seed transient (~0.3 when scaled to the plateau peak); direction against the Coulomb-off twin at equal steps: S -0.5 %, I_d -0.4 %, I_beam -0.3 %, window T_e,peak +3.2 %, window peak n_e -2.4 % - inside the shot noise of a 70 ns average at 1e17 m^-3, not a reading of the plateau hypotheses.
